title: Wrapper honours agentProvider at spawn; pause bookkeeping is per-provider
description:
SPIDR grandchild D of task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605 (architect-2e480458, 2026-09-05). dependsOn grandchild C (the store must exist to honour).

MEASURED INVARIANT: agent-provider-pause.ts:36 and agent-wrapper.ts:323-325 state ONE MOE_AGENT_COMMAND PER WRAPPER PROCESS. agent-spawner.ts:50 resolves `options.command ?? process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"] ?? "claude"` ONCE at spawnRuntime construction; agent-wrapper-main.ts:291 passes that one provider into createProviderPauseGate. The pause LEDGER is already keyed by (projectId, provider) — readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, …). Option (a) is the smallest production-reachable slice that satisfies argv[0] changing with the setting inside one wrapper; option (b) would require two wrapper processes the launcher does not start.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: per-spawn resolution (new module), spawner uses it inside attemptSpawn (codexSeat becomes per-spawn), wrapper staffing skips only the paused provider's steps, pause gate records/reads per the seat's provider, wrapper-main stops freezing one provider at process start.

NOT IN SCOPE: /sessions/read disclosure (grandchild E), UI, command kind roster.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: A test asserts argv[0] is `codex` when the durable setting says codex and `claude` when it says claude, with MOE_AGENT_COMMAND unset. The assertion is against the spawned argv, not an internal field. The codex-only env allowlist is applied for a codex spawn.
With MOE_AGENT_COMMAND set, the spawn uses it REGARDLESS of the setting. Assert argv[0] matches the env value.

Pause is per-provider: a live pause for claude does not prevent staffing a codex goal (and the reverse). A test covers a pause under this model. The comment at agent-wrapper.ts:323-325 no longer claims one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per wrapper process.
Gates quoted with `Test Files N passed`: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: INVARIANT DECISION, BINDING: option (a) PER-SPAWN RESOLUTION. The wrapper resolves the provider PER SPAWN (env > goal override > project setting > claude). Pause bookkeeping is per-provider, not per-wrapper. Do not take option (b) (one provider per process, two wrappers). Record this in the step note; a later worker must not re-decide it.

EXTRACT, DO NOT GROW. agent-spawner.ts is 438 lines and agent-wrapper-main.ts is 482 (both over the 400 cap). New agent-provider-resolve.ts owns precedence. Update the comment at agent-wrapper.ts:323-325 that currently states one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per process.
Assert spawned argv[0], not an internal field. Codex-only env allowlist (agent-spawn-environment.ts:22-24) applies when the resolved command is a codex seat.
MOE_AGENT_COMMAND still wins at spawn. Disclosure of that win on /sessions/read is grandchild E, not this row.
FEATURES ONLY. No UI, no MCP fence, no contract roster.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND BASELINE. NO EDITS. (a) CONFIRM THE PREREQUISITE LANDED. task-c851961b (grandchild C) owns the durable store and its read port; this row only HONOURS it. Prove it at the tree: `git grep -rn 'agentProvider' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v test` must show a store module with a read function, and `git grep -n 'set_agent_provider' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` must hit. If either is absent, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds ['task-c851961b968942f880950acc16dc575a'] and stop. Read that row's completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings for the EXACT read-port signature and the goalId convention (its DoD says goalId "" is the project default, a non-empty goalId is the override) rather than guessing them. (b) READ THE STRUCTURAL GAP THIS ROW'S DESCRIPTION DOES NOT MENTION, measured at HEAD f3b94eaa. `SpawnRequest` (agent-wrapper.ts:44-55) carries EXACTLY: credential, expiresAt, kind, mission, sessionId, workItemId, workspace. THERE IS NO projectId AND NO goalRef. `AgentSpawnerOptions` (agent-spawn-contract.ts:18-43) has NO store handle either. So `attemptSpawn` CANNOT resolve a per-project or per-goal setting from what it is given today - that is the real work of this row, and step 2 states the seam. (c) MEASURE THE CAPS, because two of the three files this row must edit are already over them: `wc -l` gives agent-spawner.ts 438 (OVER 400), agent-wrapper-main.ts 485 (OVER 400), agent-wrapper.ts 394 (SIX lines of headroom), agent-provider-pause.ts 186, agent-spawn-contract.ts 229. Nothing in this row may grow the first two, and agent-wrapper.ts has almost no room - the new module exists to absorb the logic. (d) NOTE THE PAUSE SHAPE: `createProviderPauseGate` is built ONCE at agent-wrapper-main.ts:287-292 with a single frozen `provider` string, and agent-wrapper.ts:326 calls `config.providerPause?.paused(...)` ONCE PER PASS, before the step loop. Per-provider pause therefore means moving that check from per-pass to per-step. (e) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. (f) `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator` - note peer dirt, never revert it.

THE RESOLVER MODULE. NEW FILE apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-resolve.ts (target <=250 lines) plus its .js bridge if this repo's convention requires one for a new orchestrator module - check a sibling (agent-provider-pause.js exists beside agent-provider-pause.ts) and follow it; a missing bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. THE SEAM, DECIDED HERE SO THE WORKER DOES NOT RE-DERIVE IT: the WRAPPER resolves the provider and puts the resolved command on the request; the SPAWNER consumes it. Reasoning, which belongs in the step note: the spawner has no store handle and no project context, while `staff()` in agent-wrapper.ts already holds `config.projectId` and the step - so resolution at the wrapper is the only place with the facts, and it keeps precedence in ONE module rather than split across two. Export `resolveAgentProvider(input)` implementing the precedence the rail binds, IN THIS ORDER: (1) `process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"]` if set - it still wins at spawn, DoD-2; (2) the per-GOAL override from the store; (3) the per-PROJECT setting; (4) the literal "claude". Take the store as an injected LAZY FACT FUNCTION, not a store handle - `(projectId, goalRef) => string | null` - matching the convention this codebase already documents three times in PlanningOfferInput ("A FACT rather than a store handle... stays pure"). That keeps this module unit-testable with no sqlite and lets wrapper-main own the composition. ALSO EXPORT the codex predicate currently inlined at agent-spawner.ts:76 (`/(?:^|[\\/])codex(?:\.[a-z]+)?$/iu`) as a named function, so the spawner imports one definition rather than keeping a second copy. Its test (agent-provider-resolve.test.ts, also new) asserts each precedence rung IN ISOLATION and, critically, each rung WINNING OVER THE ONE BELOW IT - a test that only checks "env wins" and "default is claude" leaves the middle two rungs unproven and is exactly the sweep that passes while the goal override never fires.

CARRY THE RESOLVED PROVIDER TO THE SPAWN. Two files, and the shape choice here is what keeps this row at eight files instead of fourteen. (1) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts (394 lines, SIX of headroom - do not reformat, do not grow it beyond a few lines): add `readonly provider?: string;` to `SpawnRequest` at :44-55. IT MUST BE OPTIONAL. A required field would break every existing SpawnRequest builder, and `git grep -ln 'credential:' -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator` names SIX other files that construct one (agent-authority-cleanup, agent-provider-pause.test, agent-spawn-environment.test, agent-spawner.test, agent-wrapper-reclaim.test, agent-wrapper.test). Optional keeps all six out of this row's roster. Then in `staff()`, where the request object is built at :295-298, call the resolver and set `provider`. FOR THE GOAL REF: pass `step.aggregateId` ONLY for goal-targeted steps. For a `node.deliver` step `aggregateId` is the nodeRef, NOT a goal, so there is no goal override to apply - pass null and let the project default answer. Say so in a comment; do NOT invent a node-to-goal lookup, and do not pretend the override covers node seats when it does not. (2) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts (438 lines, ALREADY OVER the 400 cap - keep this edit to a handful of lines and reformat nothing): the module-scope `const command` at :50 and `const codexSeat` at :76 become PER-SPAWN, computed inside `attemptSpawn` from `request.provider ?? options.command ?? process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"] ?? "claude"` - the trailing chain preserved verbatim so a request without a provider behaves exactly as today and every existing test stays green. Import the codex predicate from the new module rather than keeping the regex at :76. `codexSeat` then feeds the three places that already branch on it - the argv at :85, the MCP-config write at :120, and the child env at :153 - with no change to their logic.

PAUSE PER PROVIDER. (1) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-pause.ts (186 lines): the gate is constructed with ONE frozen `provider` (:36-37, :60) and its docblock at :36 states the invariant this row retires - "The provider this wrapper serves - one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per wrapper process." Change the gate so `paused(nowMs)` takes the provider to check, or so the gate is keyed per provider; the LEDGER already supports it - `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, iso)` at :66 is keyed by (projectId, provider) and needs no change, which is the measured reason option (a) is the small slice. Rewrite that docblock to state what is true afterwards: the wrapper serves MANY providers, resolved per spawn, and the pause is per (project, provider). (2) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts: the pass-level pause check at :323-330 currently short-circuits the WHOLE pass on one provider's pause, with a comment stating the same retired invariant. Move the decision into the step loop so a live claude pause skips only claude steps while a codex goal still staffs. WATCH THE 400-LINE CAP - this file is at 394. If the per-step decision needs more than a couple of lines, put the predicate in the new resolve module (or in agent-wrapper-staffing.ts, 186 lines, which already owns staffing decisions) and call it from the loop. Rewrite the :323-325 comment; DoD-3 requires it no longer claim one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per wrapper process. NOTE THE REPORTING SHAPE: `runPass` currently returns `{paused, surfaceOutcome: PROVIDER_PAUSED_OUTCOME}` for the whole pass. Decide deliberately what a pass reports when ONE provider is paused and another staffed, and say which you chose in the step note - reporting PROVIDER_PAUSED while work was staffed would make the wrapper's only operator-facing signal lie. (3) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts (485 lines, ALREADY OVER the cap - compose, do not grow): line 287-292 freezes the provider at process start via `providerFor(process.env["MOE_AGENT_COMMAND"] ?? "claude")`. Supply the store-backed lazy fact to the wrapper config instead, and stop freezing one provider. The comment at :283-286 describing the old resolution must go with it.

TESTS AGAINST THE SPAWNED ARGV. (1) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.test.ts (1090 lines, a test file so the production cap does not apply): DoD-1 and DoD-2, asserted against the SPAWNED CHILD, never an internal field - the file already has the pattern at :278, `expect(child.file).toBe("codex")`, so follow it. FOUR arms: setting says codex with MOE_AGENT_COMMAND UNSET -> `child.file` is codex AND the codex-only env allowlist applied (agent-spawn-environment.ts:22-24 is the roster; assert the child env carries the codex bearer variable and that a claude spawn does not); setting says claude -> `child.file` is claude; MOE_AGENT_COMMAND SET -> `child.file` is the env value REGARDLESS of a contrary setting (DoD-2); and no provider on the request at all -> today's behaviour, unchanged, which is the arm that proves the optional field did not silently change every existing seat. READ THE WIN32 CAVEAT AT :101 AND :181-182 BEFORE WRITING: on Windows the argv collapses into ONE shell line and `child.args` is empty, so an args-shaped assertion needs the same platform guard the neighbouring cases use. (2) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-provider-pause.test.ts (687 lines): DoD-3 - a live pause for claude does not prevent staffing a codex goal, and the reverse. Assert BOTH directions; one direction alone passes while the gate ignores the provider entirely. Assert by which step was staffed (work-item id), not by a spawn count.

DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DRILLS, recorded in the step note. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. MIXED TRACKED AND UNTRACKED HERE, so both proofs are needed and global rail 13 genuinely fires: agent-provider-resolve.ts and its test are NEW (`??`), so `git diff` is BLIND to them - back them up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id) and prove restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The six pre-existing files are tracked, so an empty `git diff -- <path>` is their proof. Say which proof applies to which path rather than applying one rule to all eight. THREE DRILLS, restore and prove after each: (i) invert the precedence so the project setting beats MOE_AGENT_COMMAND - the DoD-2 arm must go RED naming the env value it expected; this is the rung most likely to be silently wrong and the one the rail binds. (ii) Make `resolveAgentProvider` ignore the goal override and answer the project default - the goal-override rung must go RED. If it stays green, the override rung was never really tested and the arm needs fixing before you continue. (iii) Make the pause gate ignore its provider argument (answer the same pause for every provider) - the DoD-3 cross-provider arm must go RED in BOTH directions; quote both. (b) GATES - standalone foreground, one command per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting the `Test Files N passed` count line for each; an exit-0 leg with NO count line ran nothing: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row and must not be quoted as such - vitest.config.ts:32 includes no `apps/**`, so it runs zero tests against all eight files. Attribute any red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths; that intersection must be EMPTY. Disclose foreign red verbatim. Named complete_task verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. (c) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: `wc -l` agent-spawner.ts and agent-wrapper-main.ts and confirm NEITHER grew (both were already over 400 at merge-base), and agent-wrapper.ts is still under 400; a request with no `provider` still spawns exactly as before (the arm from step 5 - re-read it and confirm it would fail if the fallback chain were reordered); an unknown provider name reaching argv[0] (grandchild C refuses it at write time with AGENT_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN, but state what happens if a stale durable value survives a roster change); two concurrent spawns for different providers in one pass; a codex spawn whose env allowlist silently applied to a claude seat; the `.js` bridge present for the new module. (d) COMPLETION RECORD must state: the INVARIANT DECISION recorded verbatim so a later worker cannot re-open it - option (a), per-spawn resolution, precedence env > goal override > project setting > claude, pause per (project, provider); WHERE resolution happens (the wrapper, because the spawner has neither a store handle nor project context - name the two measurements) and that `SpawnRequest.provider` is OPTIONAL to keep six other request-building files out of this row; what a pass reports when one provider is paused and another is staffed; that the per-goal override does NOT apply to `node.deliver` seats because their aggregateId is a nodeRef, and that this is a stated limit rather than an oversight; and that the durable store is task-c851961b's, verified by grep at the delivered tree rather than re-implemented here.

comments.content:
THE ROW'S RAIL BINDS THE INVARIANT BUT NOT THE SEAM — and the seam is where the real work is. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 6 steps, 8 files (2 new).

## The structural gap the description does not name

Rail 2 says "spawner uses it inside attemptSpawn". Measured, the spawner **has nothing to resolve from**:

```
SpawnRequest      (agent-wrapper.ts:44-55)     credential, expiresAt, kind, mission,
                                               sessionId, workItemId, workspace
                                               -> no projectId, no goalRef
AgentSpawnerOptions (agent-spawn-contract.ts:18-43)  command?, environment?, spawn?, …
                                               -> no store handle
```

A worker following the rail's words alone reaches step 2 and finds `attemptSpawn` cannot see a project or a goal. So the plan decides the seam: **the wrapper resolves, the spawner consumes.** `staff()` (agent-wrapper.ts:295-298) already holds `config.projectId` and the step, and already threads `projectId` into all three mission builders — it is the only site with the facts. The spawner reads `request.provider ?? options.command ?? env ?? "claude"`, so `codexSeat` still becomes per-spawn inside `attemptSpawn` exactly as the rail requires.

## `SpawnRequest.provider` is OPTIONAL, and that is load-bearing

`git grep -ln 'credential:' -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator` names **six** other files that build a SpawnRequest (agent-authority-cleanup, plus five test files). A required field drags all six in and turns an 8-file row into 14. Optional keeps them out *and* makes the no-provider path byte-identical to today — which is what the fourth arm in step 5 exists to prove.

## Why option (a) really is the small slice

The pause **ledger is already keyed by provider**: `readProviderPause(store, projectId, provider, iso)` at agent-provider-pause.ts:66. What is frozen is the **gate**, not the ledger — built once at agent-wrapper-main.ts:287-292 and consulted **once per pass** at agent-wrapper.ts:326, before the step loop. So per-provider pause = move that check into the step loop. No ledger change at all.

## Three things a worker would otherwise hit mid-flight

1. **Two files are already over the 400-line cap** — agent-spawner.ts (438) and agent-wrapper-main.ts (485) — and **agent-wrapper.ts is at 394, six lines of headroom**, while needing a SpawnRequest field, a resolver call, and a per-step pause decision. That is why the new module exists; agent-wrapper-staffing.ts (186) is the second landing site.
2. **The per-goal override cannot cover `node.deliver` seats.** Their `step.aggregateId` is a nodeRef, not a goal, and no node→goal mapping exists. The plan states the limit and forbids inventing a lookup or passing a nodeRef where a goalRef is expected (it would silently miss every override).
3. **`runPass` reports `PROVIDER_PAUSED_OUTCOME` for the whole pass.** Once one provider can be paused while another staffs, that signal becomes ambiguous — and it is the wrapper's only operator-facing output. Step 4 requires the worker choose deliberately and say which.

## Two docblocks state the retired invariant verbatim

agent-provider-pause.ts:36 ("one MOE_AGENT_COMMAND per wrapper process") and agent-wrapper.ts:323-325. DoD-3 names only the second; the plan fixes both, or the next reader re-learns a rule this row deleted.

## Global rail 13 genuinely fires here, unlike most rows

The drill paths are **mixed**: agent-provider-resolve.ts and its test are new (`??`), so `git diff` is blind to them — SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup. The six pre-existing files are tracked — empty `git diff` is their proof. The plan requires saying which proof applies to which path rather than applying one rule to all eight.

The middle precedence rungs are the silent-failure risk: a suite proving only "env wins" and "default is claude" leaves the goal override and project setting untested. Drill (ii) exists to catch an override rung that never really fired.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 8 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE ROW'S RAIL BINDS THE INVARIANT (option (a), per-spawn resolution) BUT NOT THE SEAM, and the seam is where the real decision is. Measured: `SpawnRequest` (agent-wrapper.ts:44-55) carries NO projectId and NO goalRef, and `AgentSpawnerOptions` (agent-spawn-contract.ts:18-43) has NO store handle. So `attemptSpawn` literally cannot resolve a per-project or per-goal setting from what it is handed. A worker following the rail's words alone ("spawner uses it inside attemptSpawn") would reach step 2 and discover the spawner has nothing to resolve FROM.

CHOSEN - THE WRAPPER RESOLVES, THE SPAWNER CONSUMES. `staff()` (agent-wrapper.ts:295-298) already holds `config.projectId` and the step, and already threads `config.projectId` into all three mission builders. It adds `provider` to the request; the spawner reads `request.provider ?? options.command ?? env ?? "claude"`. `codexSeat` still becomes per-spawn inside `attemptSpawn`, satisfying the rail. Precedence lives in ONE new module.
REJECTED - injecting a store handle or a resolver into AgentSpawnerOptions: it widens the spawner's contract with project knowledge it otherwise has none of, and AgentSpawnerOptions is consumed by `claudeSpawner`/`codexSpawner` factories at agent-spawner.ts:428-435 plus every spawner test. More files, worse layering.
REJECTED - adding projectId/goalRef to SpawnRequest as REQUIRED fields: `git grep -ln 'credential:' -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator` names SIX other files that build a SpawnRequest (agent-authority-cleanup.ts, agent-provider-pause.test.ts, agent-spawn-environment.test.ts, agent-spawner.test.ts, agent-wrapper-reclaim.test.ts, agent-wrapper.test.ts). A required field drags all six into the row and turns an 8-file change into 14. ONE OPTIONAL `provider?: string` keeps them all out and makes the no-provider path byte-identical to today.
REJECTED - splitting argv resolution (DoD 1-2) from per-provider pause (DoD 3): they overlap on agent-wrapper.ts AND agent-wrapper-main.ts, so a split needs dependsOn and runs serially anyway - two claim/review cycles for one coherent invariant change, with a window where the branch resolves per-spawn while the pause still freezes one provider per process.
REJECTED - keeping the regex at agent-spawner.ts:76: exporting the codex predicate from the resolve module keeps ONE definition. Two copies of a provider-detection regex is how a codex seat gets the claude env allowlist.
REJECTED - inventing a node-to-goal lookup so the per-goal override covers node.deliver seats: no such mapping exists (aggregateId is the nodeRef). The plan states the limit instead of papering it.

6. Test files: agent-spawner.test.ts 1090, agent-provider-pause.test.ts 687 - test files are exempt from the production cap.

8. THE `.js` BRIDGE CONVENTION HOLDS in this directory: agent-provider-pause.js sits beside agent-provider-pause.ts. A new orchestrator module without its bridge kills the daemon at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

9. GATE REACH: vitest.config.ts:32 include = adapters/**, packages/**, tests/**, tools/** - no `apps/**`. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` is the only real gate for every file here.
